_comment: Which layer-A fixtures the Rust engine renders. Every fixture must appear here or in gaps; layerA/native-ready.unit.ts enforces that, so a new fixture cannot be silently skipped.

gaps.implicit-dollar-call: calls a JS-only fn (transform$) with no native$ declaration — unimplementable natively, as the census records
gaps.imported-callback: passes an imported JS function value as a callback; nothing native to call without a native$ declaration
gaps.plugin-callback: its compute() has no native$ declaration; the fixture covers the JS side of callback wire forms
gaps.global-call-setup: qwik:global.* ops have no receiver; the generator routes qwik: ops through qwik_ssr_std::call, which needs one
gaps.fragment-root: pending: the generator has no self-allocated root range for a fragment-rooted body
gaps.dynamic-tag: pending: the generator has no tagBinding branch, so a runtime tag cannot pick element or component
gaps.dynamic-tag-component: pending: the generator has no tagBinding branch, so a runtime tag cannot pick element or component
gaps.projected-slot: pending: the generator inherits the consumer slot scope for a scopeless projection, so a projected <Slot/> renders one range too many
gaps.if-setup: setup if rides the opaque js op; native needs the structured if SetupOpKind (stage 2)
gaps.fragment-tag: a keyed fragment row is a row-id collection (multi-root rows fence in <!r= ranges), which the generator does not support yet
gaps.dynamic-slot-name: pending: the generator has no dynamic-slot op, so a name expression cannot pick a projection natively
